comment: Where a new joint puts its moving side, its Offset, and a drag along its free motions (mitcad#1745, from a reported roller assembly reduced to three cylinders). Wheel (C1, Wheel:1 O1, grounded): a cylinder of diameter 60 and height 20 on the origin, Cylinder1 F1 (Body1).
Shaft (C2, Shaft:1 O2 at x = 100): a cylinder of diameter 20 and height 800, Cylinder2 F2 (Body2).
Bearing (C3, Bearing:1 O3): a cylinder of diameter 40 and height 10, Cylinder3 F3 (Body3), placed away from both by a move in the timeline (Move1 F4), as the reported bearing was.

Joint1 F5: the shaft turns in the wheel (revolute, the shaft's side on the wheel's top circle). The wheel is grounded, so the shaft moves onto its axis; without start values its turn stays nearest to where it is, and its middle (the origin of its side) stands on the wheel's top circle.

Joint2 F6, as the Joint command makes it: the shaft's side (origin A) and the bearing's bottom (origin B), cylindrical, Offset 300 mm (the parameter bearing_offset), Flip, its free motions starting at 0. The shaft is held by the grounded wheel, so the bearing moves: its bottom's middle goes onto the shaft's axis, 300 mm from the shaft's middle, and not where it was nearest.
A new Offset moves the bearing by its change.
A drag of the bearing 100 mm along the shaft's axis: kept where it is dropped (the joint's start value of tz becomes 100), although Move1 places the bearing before the joint; the shaft stays.
Recomputed again (undone and redone), the bearing stays where the drag left it; a new Offset moves it from there.

Without start values (as joints of older designs and imports), the cylindrical joint keeps its free motions nearest to where the bearing is: the offset then only shifts its slide value, and the bearing stays on the axis where it was.
